a:r.a:t: The net effect is significant: 100 C → U events/day in a mammalian cell.

p:cNvPr.descr: Deamination, shown on the left in a box. 4 reactions are shown between nucleotides. The first, at the top, is the conversion of cytosine to uracil. The cytosine is a 6-sided ring structure with the topmost C bonded up to NH2, double bonded down and left to N, which bonds down to C, which bonds down and left to O and down & right to N. N bonds straight down to C (not shown), and up and right to C. C double bonds up to C, which bonds left to the initial C. The section at the top where N double bonds to C, which bonds up to NH2, is shaded orange. An arrow to the right shows conversion to uracil. For the uracil, C double bonds up to O, bonds down and left to NH, which bonds down to C, which bonds down and left to O and down & right to N. N bonds straight down to C (not shown), and up and right to C. C double bonds up to C, which bonds left to the initial C. The NH2 has been changed to a double bonded O and the N has been changed to an NH, with the double bond removed. Below this is a reaction that converts 5-methylcytosine to thymine. The 5-methylcytosine, on the left, has the top C bonded up to NH2, double bonded down and left to N, which bonds down to C. C double bonds down and left to O and down and right to N. N bonds down to C (not shown) and up and right to C, which double bonds up to C. C bonds up and right to CH3 and up and left to the initial C. The top portion, containing the double bonded N and NH2, is shaded orange. An arrow to the right indicates conversion to thymine. The thymine has the top C double bonded up to O and bonded down and left, which bonds down to C. C double bonds down and left to O and down and right to NH. N bonds down to C (not shown) and up and right to C, which double bonds up to C. C bonds up and right to CH3 and up and left to the initial C. The section with the double bonded O and NH are shaded orange to show where the conversion occurred. Below this is the conversion of adenine to hypoxanthine. Adenine is on the left. It has 2 ring structures, one 6-sided and one 5-sided. Beginning with the apex, C bonds up to NH2, double bonds down and left to N, which bonds down to C, which double bonds down and right to N. N bonds down to C (not shown) and up & right to C. C double bonds up to C, which bonds left to the initial C. Bonded to the right of the 6-sided ring is the 5-sided ring. The apical N bonds down and left to C, which bonds down to C, which bonds right to N. N bonds down to C (not shown) up to C, which double bonds up & left to the apical N. An arrow to the right indicates conversion. To the right is hypoxanthine. It has 2 ring structures, one 6-sided and one 5-sided. Beginning with the apex, C double bonds up to O, bonds down and left to NH, which bonds down to C, which double bonds down and right to N. N bonds down to C (not shown) and up & right to C. C double bonds up to C, which bonds left to the initial C. Bonded to the right of the 6-sided ring is the 5-sided ring. The apical N bonds down and left to C, which bonds down to C, which bonds right to N. N bonds down to C (not shown) up to C, which double bonds up & left to the apical N. Below is the last example of deamination. This shows the conversion of guanine to xanthine. On the left, the guanine consists of a 5-sided ring and a 6-sided ring. The apical C on the 6-sided ring (left) double bonds up to O, bonds down and left to NH, which bonds down to C. C bonds down and left to NH2 and double bonds down and right to N. N bonds up and right to C, which double bonds up to C. C then bonds up and left to the initial C. The 5-sided ring is bonded to the right. Its apical N double bonds down and right to C, which bonds down to N. N bonds down to C (not shown) and left to C. C bonds up to C, which bonds right to the initial N. An arrow to the right indicates conversion to xanthine. The apical C on the 6-sided ring (left) double bonds up to O, bonds down and left to NH, which bonds down to C. C double bonds down and left to O and double bonds down and right to NH. N bonds up and right to C, which double bonds up to C. C then bonds up and left to the initial C. The 5-sided ring is bonded to the right. Its apical N double bonds down and right to C, which bonds down to N. N bonds down to C (not shown) and left to C. C bonds up to C, which bonds right to the initial N.
